StackType.issue: Closed 2026-07-30 (tier-2 campaign): (Task 25.) The 15 `on_stack` no-op overrides are DELETED; the base `Power.on_stack` adds, matching PowerCmd.ModifyAmount (PowerCmd.cs:236), which adds unconditionally with no StackType branch -- PowerStackType.Single means 'Amount is hidden and displayed as 1' (PowerStackType.cs:10-13), not 'does not stack'. All 16 units re-verified against their own C#: 15 are StackType.Single, and NONE overrides InstanceType (PowerModel.cs:144 default None), so none needs T1's instance machinery instead of amount-adding. Two per-site exceptions, both verified: (1) DAMPEN's C# StackType is actually `None`, not Single (DampenPower.cs:22) -- the queue's 16-unit list was wrong about it; its only applier, MagiKnight, dedupes caller-side (MagiKnight.cs:78-96: re-application calls AddCaster only and never reaches PowerCmd.Apply), so the deletion is inert through the real caller and T28's caster-set machinery is untouched and re-pinned. (2) HEX genuinely reads Amount (HexPower.cs:79 feeds CardCmd.Afflict<Hexed>(card, Amount)), so this deletion closes a real divergence that remains DORMANT only because SpectralKnight's move machine never loops back to HEX and KnightsElite fields exactly one -- a second Hex applier makes it live. ILLUSION needed no override and is unchanged (the opposite-sign case the record notes). No reachable re-application among the other 13: Burrowed and Soar re-apply only after their own expire/remove, always onto a fresh instance. Pins: test/test_stack_type_single.py (39 tests).  The text it replaced read: PowerStackType.Single, and the sim overrides on_stack to `pass` citing it. Per the settled census (`py audit/tools/power_census.py stack`, 15 such units) that reasoning is wrong: Single means "Amount is hidden and is always 1" (PowerStackType.cs:10-13), and PowerCmd.ModifyAmount (PowerCmd.cs:236) adds unconditionally with no StackType branch -- so C# really does reach Amount 2 on a second application while the sim stays at 1. Dormant because nothing reads Nemesis's Amount -- the alternation is driven by the private `_should_apply` bool (powers.py, mirroring C#'s `_shouldApplyIntangible` at NemesisPower.cs:14) and not by Amount -- and because the only ported applier, monsters/glory/test_subject.py, applies it exactly once at the phase-3 transition. Third-file citations, not hashed here. DORMANT, re-confirmed 2026-07-29 (round 11): EXECUTED -- `grep -n nemesis sts2_rl/*.py sts2_rl/**/*.py` (excluding powers.py itself) finds no reader of a `.amount`/Amount on a Nemesis instance anywhere, only the single applier at test_subject.py. Read test_subject.py directly: NemesisPower is applied inside the `elif self._respawns == 2:` branch of the boss's revive handler, a branch that can execute at most once per combat (`_respawns` only increments and the branch is keyed on an exact value), so a second application to the same Test Subject in one combat cannot happen with today's content -- no other ported monster, card, relic or potion grants NemesisPower at all. Trigger: any future NemesisPower source landing a second application on an owner already carrying one (Amount would then read 2 in C#, 1 in the sim, for whatever future listener reads it), or a second NemesisPower reader appearing that keys on Amount rather than the toggle bool.

AfterSideTurnEnd.rationale: Correct slot (Hook.AfterTurnEnd, Hook.cs:1267, CombatManager.cs:1256 -> on_enemy_side_end, combat.py). The alternation, the Intangible 1 grant and the removal on the off-beat all match NemesisPower.cs:20-35, `HasPower<IntangiblePower>` test included (powers.py). Note the removal mid-dispatch: hook_dispatch gap G7's ONLY whole-suite hit is exactly this pair -- on_enemy_side_end -> IntangiblePower x10, Nemesis removing Intangible while the dispatch walks -- and G7 records that C# makes the same call, because the PowerModel arm of CombatState.Contains (CombatState.cs:599) checks only `Owner.CombatState != null` and never that the power is still on its owner. Faithful by that already-executed cross-reference. Third-file citations, not hashed here.

guards.issue: Replaced by `if self.owner.is_dead: return` (powers.py) -- the same substitution as HighVoltage's and Territorial's, and one degree worse here, because the sim's early return also SKIPS THE TOGGLE (`_should_apply` is not flipped), so a Nemesis owner that is dead for one side end and alive for the next resumes on the wrong beat where C# would have flipped. DORMANT: the Test Subject's phase-3 Nemesis owner is the boss itself and a dead boss ends the combat (monsters/glory/test_subject.py), so no side end ever finds it dead-but-present. Trigger: Nemesis on a creature with ShouldStopCombatFromEnding or ShouldCreatureBeRemovedFromCombatAfterDeath -- i.e. an Illusion / Reattach / Adaptable / Infested / Steam Eruption / Stock / Surprise holder, all of which are ported.
